title: Sensex Tanks 900 Points, Nifty Slides Below 22,300 as RBI Hike Selloff Deepens
excerpt: Indian benchmarks extended their fall in midday trade on Thursday, October 8, a day after the RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% and shifted its stance to 'calibrated tightening.' IT heavyweights TCS, Infosys and HCLTech bucked the selloff ahead of TCS's quarterly results.
body:
• By 12:38 pm IST, the Sensex was down 889.76 points (-1.22%) at 71,748.94 and the Nifty 50 had slid 311.20 points (-1.38%) to 22,291.85, with roughly ₹10 lakh crore of investor wealth erased by early afternoon.
  • The trigger: on Wednesday the RBI raised the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — and shifted its stance from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening'. Markets now expect the repo to head toward 6% by December.
  • The selloff was broad-based: 3,176 stocks declined against 986 advancers, 235 hit fresh 52-week lows, and India VIX surged over 5%. Adani Enterprises plunged 6.57%, ITC fell 4.08% and JSW Steel shed 4.07%. IT was the lone bright spot, with TCS up 1.04%, Infosys 0.75% and HCLTech 0.66% ahead of TCS's quarterly results after market hours.
  • What it means for you: Geojit Investments sees two more 25bp hikes in this cycle, which would push home and personal loan rates higher (better rates for FD savers). The rupee held just above 96.70 to the dollar, near record lows, and foreign investors sold ₹6,121 crore of Indian equities in a single day on Wednesday.

Indian equities deepened their fall in midday trade on Thursday, October 8, as investors absorbed the Reserve Bank of India's surprise rate hike and weak global cues. The Sensex and Nifty both fell more than 1% by early afternoon, with broad-based selling dragging the indices closer to key technical support zones and wiping out roughly ₹10 lakh crore of investor wealth.

Context & Background

The selloff is the market's verdict on Wednesday's RBI decision: a 25-basis-point repo rate hike to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023, accompanied by a shift in stance from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening'. Chief Investment Strategist Dr. V K Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments said the move has direct market implications — and flagged that more is coming.

On Wednesday, the Sensex had already fallen 429.11 points to close at 72,638.70 and the Nifty 50 ended down 173.05 points at 22,603.05 as the rate-hike strategy pivot took hold. Overnight, Wall Street retreated — the Dow Jones fell 0.66% while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each shed 0.22% — as the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.37% in intraday trade, its highest in decades. Brent crude hovered above $101 a barrel, and the rupee slid 36 paise on Wednesday to close at 96.78 against the dollar, its second-weakest close on record. Foreign investors sold ₹6,121.37 crore of Indian equities in a single day.

Thursday's session opened lower — the Sensex at 72,668.00 and the Nifty at 22,599.05 — and the slide accelerated through the morning. By 10:49 am the Sensex was down 426.81 points at 72,211.89; by noon it had fallen 731.77 points to 71,906.93 with the Nifty at 22,349.65.

Impact & Analysis

The midday damage was extensive. Market breadth on the BSE was heavily negative, with 3,176 stocks declining against just 986 advancing. A total of 235 stocks hit fresh 52-week lows against 113 touching 52-week highs, and the Nifty's advance-decline ratio stood at a lopsided 8:42.

Adani Enterprises was the Nifty's worst performer, plunging 6.57% to ₹2,562.90, with group peer Adani Ports down 3.97% to ₹1,680.70. ITC tumbled 4.08% to ₹254.85, JSW Steel shed 4.07% to ₹1,180.00 and Max Healthcare fell 3.76%. Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank were the top contributors to the Nifty's overall decline. Nifty Metal was the worst-performing sectoral index, extending Wednesday's 2.35% fall, while Nifty Realty came under sharp pressure as higher borrowing costs weighed on interest-rate-sensitive stocks. Barring IT, every major sectoral index was trading in the red.

The lone bright spot was the IT sector. TCS held gains of 1.04% at ₹2,102.00 ahead of its Q2 FY27 results due after market hours — the bellwether kicks off earnings season — while Infosys rose 0.75% to ₹999.40 and HCL Technologies added 0.66% to ₹1,192.80. On the commodity front, MCX crude oil rose 1.72% to ₹8,700, tracking WTI near $90, and MCX gold gained 0.39% to ₹149,689.

"With two more rate hikes of 25bp each likely in this rate hiking cycle, there will be pressure on valuations rising from higher fixed income returns."

— Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, the session carries a mixed signal. The rupee hovering just above 96.70 to the dollar — near its weakest on record — means dollars remitted home buy more rupees, softening the blow for those with rupee-denominated obligations. But sustained foreign-investor selling and a rising-rate cycle are classic headwinds for Indian equities, and diaspora portfolios with Indian exposure should expect continued volatility until the rate path clarifies. The broader global backdrop — surging U.S. yields, crude above $100 — is the same pressure driving money out of emerging markets across the board.

What's Next

TCS reports its Q2 FY27 results after market hours on Thursday, kicking off earnings season; attention will be on its outlook and AI spending commentary, with Infosys and HCLTech reporting in the coming days. Technically, the Nifty's next key support lies in the 22,190–22,210 band — a breach could expose 22,020–22,040 — while 22,500–22,520 remains stiff resistance. For the Sensex, support is at 71,500 and resistance at 72,400. With the RBI's December meeting now expected to bring the repo toward 6%, markets will watch every RBI signal — and every inflation print — until the rate path is clear.
